theme.title: The Numbers Game
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: How many regular-season games did the 2013–14 champion Spurs win?
questions.context: San Antonio · the Beautiful Game title
questions.note: 62 wins before the rematch with Miami.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the best record in the league at 62–20

funFacts.text: San Antonio entered the season with a then-record ten international players.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: an NBA-record ten international players

funFacts.text: The Spurs had lost their first NBA Finals series the prior year.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: marking the first time the Spurs lost in the NBA Finals

funFacts.text: Gregg Popovich led the team as both coach and president.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Head coach | Gregg Popovich

questions.prompt: Rick Barry set the first NBA record for threes in a game in February 1980. How many did he make?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Barry would later set the original 3-point record at 8 in a single game on February 9, 1980 against the Utah Jazz.

funFacts.text: Barry's final season overlapped with Larry Bird's Boston debut; both were present for an early NBA three.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Rick Barry of the Houston Rockets, in his final season, also made one in the same game

funFacts.text: Julius Erving made the only three of the entire 1980 NBA Finals, showing how rare the shot still was.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: In the 1980 NBA Finals, Julius Erving made the only three of the series

funFacts.text: In one 1980 Finals game, neither team even attempted a three-pointer.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: in Game 4, neither team attempted a single shot beyond the arc

questions.prompt: Golden State opened the second half of Game 2 of the 2019 Finals with how many unanswered points?
questions.note: 18, the most to start a half in Finals history.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Warriors' 18 unanswered points to begin the second half were the most in NBA Finals history to start a half.

funFacts.text: Klay Thompson's night ended after he landed awkwardly while attempting a three and injured his hamstring.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Thompson left the game in the fourth quarter with a left hamstring injury

funFacts.text: Andre Iguodala hit a late outside shot to prevent Toronto's comeback from forcing another ending.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Iguodala cemented the win with a three-pointer with 5.9 seconds remaining

funFacts.text: DeMarcus Cousins made a rare Finals start and added rebounds and assists after returning from injury.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Cousins, who was moved into the starting lineup, had 11 points, 10 rebounds and six assists

questions.prompt: How many points did Gus Williams score in overtime Game 4 of the 1979 Finals?
questions.note: 36 points in a pivotal overtime win.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: May 29 Washington W 114–112 (OT) Gus Williams (36)

funFacts.text: The game needed overtime before Seattle escaped with a win.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)

funFacts.text: John Johnson dished out 13 assists in the same Game 4.

funFacts.text: The victory put Seattle one win away from the championship.

questions.prompt: When Kyrie Irving hit 'The Shot' over Steph Curry in the 2016 Finals Game 7, how many seconds remained?
questions.context: Kyrie Irving · Cavaliers at Warriors · 2016 Finals
questions.note: 53 seconds remained. The shot gave Cleveland the late lead in its 3–1 comeback.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
